## Which observations describe the treatment response? {#response-unit .interaction}


<p class="prompt-tag">Carry the design into the data · 2 minutes in pairs</p>
<p class="medium">“We now understand the experiment.<br>Before testing anything, what actually happened?”</p>
<div class="allocation">
<div><p>One value per tube</p><p class="small">The three assay aliquots have already been summarized.</p></div>
<div><p>One change per preparation</p><p class="small">Compound Q minus its paired vehicle.</p></div>
</div>
<p class="takeaway fragment">Six preparations contribute six paired changes.</p>


::: notes
**Time: 01:18–01:23 (5 minutes).**

**Say:** The opening block is complete. Use the five minutes before the planned break to connect its design to the observations we will describe. Give pairs two minutes to identify the relevant change and three minutes to debrief. Each tube contributes the arithmetic average of its three technical readings; no aliquots were omitted. Each preparation then supplies one Q-minus-vehicle comparison. This preprocessing respects the simple balanced assay design. The term average is familiar language here; its definition comes later. Ask which experimental space the six preparations cover. No result is revealed until after the break.

**Conceptual point:** The six biological responses are paired changes. Twelve tube summaries are their ingredients; 36 technical readings are not 36 treatment responses.

**Likely misconception:** Summarizing assay repeats loses six biological experiments or establishes independence. The original raw readings remain available, and the dependence caveat from the earlier block still applies.

**Optional follow-up:** Which count belongs beside a summary of the treatment response?

**Sources:** AppliedStats_2026.pdf pp. 73–74, 121–122, adapted to the current protocol. Bridge completes the population block before the break.

:::

## A pause before we look at the data {#session-break .break-slide}


<p class="big">15-minute break</p>
<p class="small keyline">Then: what do the data actually look like?</p>


::: notes
**Time: 01:23–01:38 (15 minutes).**

**Say:** Pause for the full 15 minutes. Resume the session at elapsed time 01:38. This is a break screen, not a core teaching slide.

**Conceptual point:** Preserve the planned break and separation between establishing the experiment and describing its results.

**Likely misconception:** Break time is additional lecture time. Do not fill it with extra course material.

**Optional follow-up:** No audience task during the break.

**Sources:** COURSE_OUTLINE.md: planned mid-session break (now 01:23–01:38).

:::
